COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No.2965 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate for the 
petitioners.
Mr. Devendra Bohra, Standing 
Counsel for the State.
It is the claim of the petitioners that 
they had given certain land to the Tehri 
Hydro Development Corporation, but now, 
State Government is intending to allot 
certain land to the displaced persons, and, 
while doing that exercise, State authorities 
are encroaching upon the land, which is 
under the possession of the petitioners. 
Learned counsel for the petitioners 
would submit that, in fact, in the year 
2020, a joint survey was conducted and 
lands have been demarcated, as given in 
Annexure No.8.
Let learned State Counsel get 
instructions as to what is the basis of the 
allotment. Are State authorities following 
the joint survey conducted in the year 
2020, which is Annexure No.8? And if not, 
how had they demarcated their own lands? 
List this matter on 20.10.2023, just 
after fresh cases. 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
18.10.2023

21.12.2023 WPMS No. 2965 of 2023
Sri Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. V.K. Kohli, learned Senior Counsel assisted 
by Mr. Birendra Singh Adhikari, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Davendra Singh Bohra, learned Standing 
Counsel for the State.
3. Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned Senior Counsel 
assisted by Mr. Siddhartha Sah, learned counsel for 
the applicants in Intervention Application (IA No.03 of 
2023).
4. Mr. Dobhal submits that he is appearing on 
behalf of the applicants, to whom the land has been 
allotted, and the possession has been given.
5. Let the District Magistrate, Haridwar, as well as 
the Director, Directorate Tehri Dam Rehabilitation 
Project, New Tehri, may file their personal affidavits 
within a week, giving description of the land, which 
was allotted to the displaced persons, alongwith all the 
orders passed by the Revenue Courts, and the Civil 
Courts, the reference of which, has been given, in the 
instructions submitted by the Director, Directorate 
Tehri Dam Rehabilitation Project, New Tehri by his 
letter dated 19.10.2023, which is addressed to the 
Chief Standing Counsel.
6. Learned State Counsel submits that there is no 
disclosure of the decisions passed in several disputes, 
which were adjudicated by the Revenue Court.
7. The General Manager (HR & Tax), BHEL, is also  directed to file his personal affidavit, giving therein the 
reasons as to why he has not disclosed the outcome of 
the cases, which were adjudicated by the Revenue 
Courts.
8. Put up this matter on 03.01.2024, as a first 
case.
9. Registry is directed to keep this matter under 
the caption “part-heard”.
10. Mr. Dobhal submits that, as on date, no
construction is going on over the land, which is allotted 
to the interveners.
11. The instructions supplied by the learned 
Standing Counsel, are also placed on record. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 21.12.2023

IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND 
AT NAINITAL
HON’BLE JUSTICE SRI RAKESH THAPLIYAL
January 3, 2024
Writ Petition No. 2965 of 2023 (M/S)
Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited …..…….Petitioner 
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & Ors. ….…Respondents.
Counsel for the Petitioners: Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate 
assisted by Mr. B.S. Adhikari
Counsel for the State: Mr. Devendra Singh Bohra, Standing 
Counsel
Counsel for the applicants Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Senior Advocate 
assisted by Mr. Siddhartha Sah and 
Mr. Shubhang Dobhal
Upon hearing the learned Counsel, the Court made the following Order: 
1. By the instant writ petition, the petitioner is praying 
for the following reliefs:-
(i) A writ order or direction in the nature of certiorari 
quashing the impugned order dated 05.10.2023 
(Annexure-10) passed by the DM Haridwar.
(ii) A writ order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus directing the District Magistrate Haridwar to 
follow the demarcation done earlier on 14.09.2020
(Annexure-8) of the land of BHEL admeasuring 13.4 
hectare in Khasra No. 451.
2. Mr. V.K. Kohli, learned Senior Advocate submits 
that there is no relevancy of the order dated 17.01.2019, 
passed by the Assistant Collector-1st and the order dated 
22.06.2010 passed by Chief Revenue Officer in Revision 
No. 3/2008-09.
3. Mr. V.K. Kohli, learned Senior Advocate assisted by 
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, learned counsel for the petitioner 
submits that the land falling in Khasra No. 451 
measuring 21.07 hectare was acquired for BHEL in the 
year 1962 out of which 8.3 hectare land was released in 
the favour of the Irrigation Department, and, as such,  2
remaining 13.4 hectare was still with the possession of 
the BHEL.
4. In this writ petition, intervention application is 
moved by those who are displaced persons, as their land 
were acquired for construction of Tehri Dam Project. It is 
contended by the learned Senior Advocate Mr. Rajendra 
Dobhal, who is representing the interveners that under 
Rehabilitation Policy of the Government applicants are 
legally entitled for plot of 200 meters for residential 
purpose and half acre of the land is for the agricultural 
purposes. It is submitted by the learned senior advocate 
for the intervener that the applicants were allotted plot of 
200 meters for construction of their houses and half acre 
of land for agricultural purposes by the Director 
Rehabilitation by order dated 29.06.2010, but, despite 
the aforesaid orders of allotment and possession over the 
plots, which were allotted to the interveners were not 
given by the Director Rehabilitation. Consequently, writ 
petitions were preferred before this Court bearing WPMS 
No. 2110 of 2010, WPMS No. 1870 of 2010, WPMS No. 
2273 of 2010 and WPMS No. 305 of 2011. All these writ 
petitions were clubbed together and decided by this 
Court by judgment and order dated 27.04.2012, which 
the interveners has enclosed with the intervention 
application. All these writ petitions were allowed and 
mandamus were issued to handover the possession of 
the agriculture plots, as detailed in the allotment order 
dated 29.06.2010, within a period of eight weeks from 
the date of production of a certified copy of the order 
before the Director Rehabilitation, Tehri Project, New 
Tehri. It is submitted that despite the order of this Court, 
possession were not given. Thereafter, a contempt 
petition being CLCON No. 10 of 2013 was preferred  3
before this Court wherein Mr. Ranjeet Kumar Sinha, Addl. 
Secretary Department of Home and Mr. Y.K. Pant, 
Director Rehabilitation, New Tehri were present in 
person. The operative para of the order dated 
13.07.2015, passed in the said contempt application is 
being extracted hereunder:-
“Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, Chief Standing Counsel for 
the State of Uttarakhand and both the officers present in 
court submitted that actual possession of the allotted plots 
could not be handed over to the contempt applicants 
because of pendency of civil litigation between BHEL and 
THDC. They further contended that if civil case is decided in 
favour of the THDC, possession of the allotted plots to the 
contempt applicants shall be delivered immediately after 
pronouncement of judgment. They further contended that in 
the event, case is decided against the THDC i.e. in favour of 
the BHEL appropriate alternative developed plots of the 
same dimensions in the same locality shall be allotted to the 
contempt applicants within fifteen days after pronouncement 
of judgment by the trial court and actual possession shall be 
handed over to the contempt applicants forthwith.”
5. It is contended that in compliance of the 
undertaking given in the contempt proceedings, now, the
allotment has been made by the District Magistrate by 
order dated 05.10.2023, which has been assailed in the 
present writ petition.
6. As it appears from the order passed in the contempt 
petition, a statement was given that actual possession of 
the allotted plots could not be handed over due to the 
pendency of the civil litigation between BHEL and THDC. 
It was also contended that if civil case is decided in 
favour of the THDC, possession of the allotted plots to
the contempt applicants shall be delivered immediately  4
after pronouncement of judgment. It is also stated that if 
case is decided against the THDC, i.e., in favour of the 
BHEL appropriate alternative developed plots of the same 
dimension in the same locality shall be allotted to the 
contempt applicants within fifteen days.
7. Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned Senior Advocate for 
the intervenors submits that civil litigation which was 
pending between THDC and BHEL in O.S No. 196 of 
2010, preferred by the BHEL for seeking permanent 
injunction against THDC was dismissed on 21.11.2019 
and while deciding the said suit, issue no. 2 was framed, 
which reads as under:-

9. Against the judgment dated 21.11.2019, passed in 
O.S. No. 21 of 2010, a Civil Appeal No. 114 of 2019 was  5
preferred by the BHEL before the 5th Addl. District Judge, 
Haridwar and the said appeal was dismissed by judgment 
and order dated 05.12.2022. 
10. Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned Senior Advocate for 
the intervenors submits that the order whereby the 
appeal preferred by the BHEL was dismissed is not 
enclosed in the writ petition.
11. In para 10 of the writ petition there is a reference of 
the judgment rendered by the Civil Court in O.S. No. 19 
of 2010 and further statement has been given that 
against the judgment of the Civil Court as well as of the 
Appellate Court, BHEL is preparing to file an appeal.
12. It is submitted by Mr. V.K. Kohli, learned Senior 
Advocate assisted by Mr. B.S. Adhikari, learned counsel
for the petitioner that after filing of the writ petition a 
second appeal, i.e. SA No. 181 of 2023, has been 
preferred by the BHEL which is a time barred appeal and 
is still in the Registry of this Court.
13. As it appears from the order passed by the Civil 
Judge (Jr. Div.) dated 21.11.2019 wherein issue no. 2 
was dealt with that it was the case of the THDC that they 
were in possession of Khasra No. 451 measuring 8.3 
hectare. The order impugned which was passed by the 
District Magistrate dated 05.10.2023, reveals that the 
allotment were done in respect of Khasra No. 451 part of 
which, as per the judgment rendered by the Civil Court,
is in possession of the THDC.
14. Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned Senior Advocate for 
the intervenors vehemently disputing that the order
dated 17.01.2019, passed by the Assistant Collector-1st 6
Class and the order dated 22.06.2010 passed by Chief 
Revenue Officer in Revision No. 3/2008- has no 
relevance, as contended by the learned counsel for the 
petitioner, and submits that these orders are also 
relevant because this is in respect of the same land 
which was meant for the allottees, was the subject 
matter of the said revenue suit, which was also decided 
against the BHEL against which revision was also filed 
and the revision was also dismissed and thereafter writ 
petition was also preferred but the writ petition was also 
dismissed on the basis that proceedings are summary in 
nature and writ petition is not maintainable but that 
orders have not been brought on record.
15. All these aspects are required to be considered after 
inviting counter affidavit.
16. Respondent(s) may file counter affidavit within four 
weeks. Two weeks’ thereafter is granted to the learned 
counsel for the petitioner to file rejoinder affidavit. 
17. The learned counsel for the petitioner may file 
objection to the intervention application within a period 
of four weeks.
18. List in the week commencing 26.02.2024.
19. The interim relief application will be heard on that 
day.
__________________ 
RAKESH THAPLIYAL, J.
Parul

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No.2965 of 2023
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. V.K. Kohli, learned senior 
counsel, assisted by Mr. Birendra Singh 
Adhikari, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Yogesh Tiwari, learned 
Standing counsel for the State.
3. Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned 
Senior counsel, assisted by Mr. 
Siddhartha Sah and Mr. Shubhang 
Dobhal, learned counsel for the 
respondent.
3. The Coordinate Bench of this 
Court, in the earlier round of litigation,
in a writ petition filed by the BHEL, i.e. 
WPMS No.1309 of 2010, dismissed the 
petition, which was arising out of a 
proceeding initiated under Section 41 of 
the L.R. Act by giving a liberty to the 
petitioner to file a regular suit under 
Section 40-A of the Land Revenue Act. 
This judgment was rendered by the 
Coordinate Bench on 22.08.2023. 
Thereafter, the present writ petition was
filed on 17.10.2023, and
simultaneously, an application was also
filed on 28.07.2024 under Section 41 of 
the Land Revenue Act before the 
concerned Sub-Divisional Magistrate. As 
it appears from the judgment passed by 
the Coordinate Bench dated 22.08.2023 
only this much liberty was given to the 
petitioner BHEL to file a regular suit 
under Section 40-A of the Land Revenue 
Act, but surprisingly without availing  said liberty, this petition has been filed 
with the following reliefs:-
“1. A writ order or direction in the nature of 
Certiorari quashing the impugned order dated 
05.10.2023 (Annexure-10) passed by the DM 
Haridwar.
2. A writ order or direction in the nature of 
Mandamus directing the District Magistrate 
Haridwar to follow the demarcation done earlier on 
14.09.2020 (Annexure-8) of the land of BHEL of 
13.4 hectare in Khasra No.451.
2A-A writ order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus directing the respondents to demolish 
the construction raised by them in the land subject 
matter of writ petition bearing Khasra no.451, 
which has been shown in the plan (Annexure No.1 
of supplementary affidavit dated 16.04.2024 
attached with IA/8/2024).”
5. Not only this, there was another 
litigation in between the BHEL and 
THDC, and that was arising out of a civil 
suit filed by the BHEL against the THDC 
for seeking permanent injunction 
bearing Civil Suit No. 196 of 2010, 
which was dismissed on 21.11.2019,
and in that suit, the issue No.1 was very 
vital and material, which was decided 
against the BHEL.
6. Against the aforesaid judgment, a 
regular civil appeal was filed by the 
BHEL before the District Judge, 
Haridwar, bearing Civil Appeal No.114 of 
2019, which was also dismissed on 
05.12.2022.
7. Being aggrieved with the order 
passed in the civil suit as well as in the 
appeal, the BHEL further filed a second 
appeal, and it has been informed to this 
Court that it is a time barred second 
appeal, which has yet not been 
admitted.
8. These are the two litigations. Now  it is very surprising that despite the 
liberty given to the BHEL to file a 
regular suit under Section 40-A of the 
Land Revenue Act, the BHEL has 
decided to avail the remedy to file a writ 
petition under Article 226 of the 
Constitution of India. It is very 
surprising that instead of availing the 
liberty, as given by the High Court for 
filing a regular suit, the present writ 
petition has been filed, wherein the 
issue of title is being raised.
9. Now, as on today, neither the 
regular suit has been filed, as per the 
liberty given by the Coordinate Bench,
nor the second appeal has yet been 
admitted. Now the question is as to 
whether issue of title can be adjudicated 
in the present writ petition, which has 
been preferred under Article 226 of the 
Constitution of India?
10. Mr. Yogesh Tiwari, learned 
Standing Counsel for the State and Mr. 
Rajendra Dobhal, learned Senior 
counsel assisted by Mr. Siddhartha Sah, 
Advocate, submits that the instant writ 
petition has been filed without any 
cause of action and, moreover, the 
judgment passed by the Coordinate 
Bench in WPMS No.1309 of 2010, was 
also suppressed, and it appears that it 
was a deliberate suppression of facts. 
11. It has also been informed to this 
Court that the second appeal was 
preferred after filing the present writ 
petition. What it reveals for one cause of 
action as of now the BHEL availed three 
remedies, i.e. one civil suit, application 
moved under Section 41 of the LR Act, which, in fact, was already decided and 
the 3rd one is the instant present writ 
petition preferred under Article 226 of 
the Constitution of India. 
12. Put up this matter for further 
argument on 18.03.2025.
13. Interim order is extended till the 
next date of listing.

direction to the District Magistrate, Haridwar, to follow the

2. Annexure-8 (Page 116-119) is the demarcation report along

6. Thereafter being aggrieved with the proceeding initiated 
under Section 41 of L.R. Act and the order of Deputy Collector
dated 17.01.2009 as well as the order of Board of Revenue dated 
22.06.2010, the BHEL preferred a writ petition (MS) No. 1309 of 
2010 before this court, which was dismissed on 22.08.2023 by 
observing that proceeding under challenge is summary 
proceedings i.e. proceeding under Section 41 of L.R. Act and as 
such the writ petition would not be maintainable and only
recourse available to the petitioner (BHEL) would be to resort the 
proceeding under Section 40A of L.R. Act. While dismissing the 
writ petition the Coordinate Bench also give liberty to the 
petitioner (BHEL) to avail the remedy as providing under Section 
40A of L.R. Act.
7. The order passed by the Coordinate Bench dated 22.08.2023 
in WPMS No. 1309 of 2010 was never been assailed by the 
petitioner (BHEL) and as such attains finality, however, it has 
been informed that the petitioner (BHEL) availed the liberty after 
filing of the instant writ petition, however, Mr. Rajendra Dobhal 
pointed out that instead of availing remedy under Section 40A 
again the BHEL availed remedy under Section 41 of L.R. Act, 
though the proceeding under Section 41 of L.R. Act already 
attains finality by the judgment dated 22.08.2023, which was 
never been challenged. 4

in which the BHEL was one of the party, therefore, the BHEL is 
directed to place the report of Revenue Inspector dated 28.04.2008
as well as report of Tehsildar dated 13.06.2008 along with Naksha
